UnitStatement: This document defines the IP and Data Boundary Policy for the project.
The policy keeps the public OpenPipeStress repository aligned with the project intent of public open mechanics with private/user-supplied code and proprietary data.
This policy is a project governance control, not legal advice, professional engineering approval, certification, sealing, standards-body endorsement, or a code-compliance claim.
Human or legal review remains required when redistribution rights or protected-content status are uncertain.
This draft policy is aligned to execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 and approved DAG-006 coordination authority.
The project license has been selected as PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0.
Contribution-source license and redistribution fields record the source basis for submitted material and do not replace the project license notice.

The final contributor legal mechanism, maintainer roster/quorum, release authority, legal-review authority, security contact, release-label vocabulary, human-acceptance workflow, and jurisdiction-specific professional-practice wording remain TBD until recorded by the human project authority or qualified reviewer.
The public repository may contain solver algorithms based on open mechanics.
The public repository may contain geometry, unit, load, stress-recovery, and report schemas.
The public repository may contain blank templates and private-library import mechanisms.
The public repository may contain invented example data with clear notices.
The public repository may contain public-domain or permissively licensed data with documented provenance.
The public repository may contain validation benchmarks from original, public-domain, or permissively licensed sources.
The public repository may contain review checklists, manifests, and empty schema slots that help users record private/code-specific data without bundling those values publicly.
The public repository must not contain ASME or other standards-body code text, tables, figures, examples, or commentary.
The public repository must not contain material allowable tables copied from standards.
The public repository must not contain B31J stress-intensification or flexibility-factor content copied from standards.
The public repository must not contain B16/B36/MSS/ISO/EN/CSA dimensional or rating tables copied from standards.
The public repository must not contain proprietary vendor catalogs without redistribution rights.
The public repository must not contain commercial software examples, report templates, or benchmark files without permission.
The public repository must not contain user private rule packs, owner standards, or company design bases.

The public repository must not contain code-specific load combinations, allowables, SIFs, flexibility factors, acceptance criteria, or owner requirements unless they are invented examples or otherwise cleared for public redistribution.
Every public data record must include the required provenance fields.
The source_name provenance field records a human-readable source.
The source_location provenance field records a URL, path, or document identifier, or TBD.
The source_license provenance field records the redistribution basis, or TBD.
The contributor provenance field records the person or org submitting.
The contributor_certification provenance field is a statement that data is not copied from a protected source unless licensed.
The redistribution_status provenance field is one of public_permissive, private_only, unknown, or protected_suspected.
The review_status provenance field is one of pending, accepted, rejected, or quarantined.

Records with source_license = TBD, redistribution_status = unknown, or missing contributor certification are not acceptable as public data and remain pending, private-only, rejected, or quarantined until a maintainer records a review disposition.
If data appears to derive from a protected standard or proprietary source, agents and maintainers must stop ingestion.
Under the quarantine rule, agents and maintainers must mark the record protected_suspected.
Under the quarantine rule, the artifact must be moved to quarantine/protected-content/ or another maintainer-approved non-example quarantine path.
Under the quarantine rule, the issue must be recorded.
Under the quarantine rule, human or legal review must be requested.
Quarantined material must not be used as public fixture data, copied into documentation, summarized into public tables, or converted into public defaults while its status is unresolved.

Private material libraries, rule packs, component catalogs, and owner design bases belong in user-controlled private paths; the public project may provide schemas and importers but must not assume those files are redistributable.

Importers, examples, reports, telemetry, and issue templates must default to excluding private project, material, component, rule-pack, owner-standard, and company design-basis data unless a user intentionally exports or contributes it with documented redistribution rights.
Generated reports may reference a user rule-pack ID, version, checksum, and source note.
Public report templates must not embed protected formulas or tables.
Users are responsible for private report templates that quote licensed standards.

Public contributions that add data, examples, report templates, schemas with example payloads, benchmark cases, import fixtures, or documentation excerpts must be reviewed against governance/CONTRIBUTION_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md before acceptance.
The contribution review checklist records contribution identity and scope.
The contribution review checklist records source, provenance, license, redistribution, and contributor certification evidence.
The contribution review checklist records protected-content and private-data risk.
The contribution review checklist records test, validation, and documentation evidence.
The contribution review checklist records reviewer disposition.
The contribution review checklist records quarantine or escalation record when needed.
Maintainers may reject or defer contributions that do not provide enough evidence to satisfy this policy.
Acceptance of repository content is project governance only and is not professional approval of engineering use.
